name: neuroimaging modalities overview
title: Choosing a neuroimaging modality: different objects need different kinds of resolution (spatial, contrast, temporal); radiography, fluoroscopy and CT use X-rays, ultrasound and MRI do not, and each trades its resolution against cost, availability, invasiveness, radiation and scan length; below, what each MRI sequence (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, SWI) shows and the order of imaging in a suspected stroke

root.title: Which modality best RESOLVES the object of interest?
lines: SPATIAL: tell apart nearby objects · CONTRAST: tell apart objects of similar density · TEMPORAL: see change over time

panels.title: MRI: choose the sequence
items: T1, 'anatomic': fluid DARK · structural abnormality · enhancement with contrast
T2, 'pathologic': fluid WHITE ('water is white on T2') · edema
FLAIR: fluid white EXCEPT CSF (inversion recovery suppresses it) · edema stands out
DWI / ADC map: RESTRICTED water diffusion · a measure of cellularity · T2-weighted
SWI: BLOOD products (hemoglobin in its oxidation states, hemosiderin)
advanced: MR angiography · MR perfusion · MR spectroscopy · functional MRI

panels.title: Putting it to work: a suspected stroke, in order
items: 3 · catheter angiography (fluoroscopy, digital subtraction) + thrombectomy to pull the clot
